## Destructive action state contract

### Decision sequence

1. **Availability first.** Determine whether the selected record may be deleted and expose the reason and corrective action when it may not.
2. **Input feedback second.** Pointer hover, keyboard focus, and press are visual feedback only; they never change deletion eligibility or operation state.
3. **Commit atomically.** On the first valid activation, set `isSubmitting` before starting the request.
4. **Resolve locally.** Success removes or marks only the affected record; failure keeps its context and exposes an adjacent retry path.

| state and trigger | status | reason | remediation | evidence | provenance |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ready` semantic state; selection is deletable and no request is active | pass | The action is available without implying it is harmless. | Render the native destructive `<button>` with its existing destructive token treatment. | `disabled` is absent; the activation handler accepts input only while `isSubmitting === false`. | Native button semantics; existing destructive semantic tokens. |

## Async destructive action contract

Use one real `<button type="button">` for the destructive action. Its visual state is a presentation of the semantic state; it must never be the source of truth.

| Semantic state | Trigger and ownership | Visual state | Behavior and semantics | Exit / recovery |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Ready | The item is eligible and no request is in flight. | Destructive button at rest. | Pointer click and `Enter`/`Space` invoke the same guarded submit function. | Submit begins only after the guard accepts it. |
